submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on the completion-side token of a locally highly constrained bigram: most strongly on a single-character separator (the standalone space immediately before a digit, ( right after range, > closing a tag, or the space after = or >) where the preceding token opens a slot with a nearly determined filler such as a number after to, by, at, =, >, range, or a numbered name like Apollo, and at mid strength on the fixed second word of a memorized phrase (than after greater, of after capital, bank after central, noon after at). The same separator or function word in an unconstrained context (a space before a non-number, of after ordinary nouns, than after other comparatives, ( after other verbs) drives little or no activation, which beats a pure token-identity account; weak blips on ordinary content words (announced, he, triangle, began) are acknowledged leftovers near baseline.
